metadata.neutral_citation: LAM CHI FAT v. SO KAM SUI, KENNETH AND ANOTHER [1995] HKCFI 565; HCPI 167/1994 (26 October 1995)
metadata.case_name: LAM CHI FAT v. SO KAM SUI, KENNETH AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Fracture of the left wrist (ulnar styloid) with associated damage to the triangular fibro-cartilage complex (TFCC)
source: Dr. Chiang therefore x-rayed the plaintiff's left wrist, revealing a fracture which he said was likely to have been caused in the accident.

this fracture was unlikely to unite because of an associated injury to a cartilage structure close to the fractured bone - the ulnar styloid. The area of this cartilage system, known together with the ulnar styloid as the triangular fibro-cartilage complex or TFCC, was described by Dr. Chiang as one of the most difficult in orthopaedic surgery.
Dr. Chiang assessed the permanent impairment of the plaintiff's left wrist at 8%.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture at other specified part of wrist or hand level

injuries.description: Fractured rib (as described in Employees' Compensation Assessment Board certificates)
source: The certificates in either case described the injuries as a fractured rib with left wrist injury and pain.
tenderness to the chest wall and left wrist and abrasions to the right leg.
injuries.icd_description: Abrasion of other or unspecified parts of lower leg

manifestations.description: pain and weakness in the left wrist
numbness in his hand which prevented him holding onto scaffolding
could not hold a bowl of soup for long without needing to put it down
relatively small loss of power in the grip
permanent impairment of the plaintiff's left wrist at 8%
unable to return to his former employment as a painter

treatments_received: physiotherapy at South Kwai Chung Polyclinic
